A new private equity vehicle from the Bajaj Finserv group has closed its first round of capital at INR 950 crore and plans to build Grade A offices alongside established developers. The fund is targeting a final close of INR 2,000 crore and will use equity joint ventures rather than the debt-led models common in Indian real estate funding. Executives said demand from global capability centres and other large occupiers is a key tailwind, and the platform sees the fund as the base for a broader alternatives business.

Bajaj Finserv's alternative investment platform, Bajaj Alternate Investment Management (Bajaj Alts), said on Monday that it has raised INR 950 crore for real estate investments. The amount is the initial close of the Bajaj Alts Real Estate - Growth Fund I, the platform's first fund. The company is targeting a final close of INR 2,000 crore, with a greenshoe option that would let it accept commitments above the base target. According to an official statement, the fund has a strong pipeline of investment opportunities that it is currently evaluating, although the statement did not name any projects, developers or cities where the capital will be deployed. The fund will invest using an approach followed by global funds, which involves partnering with leading developers through equity joint ventures (JVs) to develop Grade A commercial office assets in prime markets. Sanchit Bhatia, head of the real estate fund at Bajaj Alts, said it will partner with established developers to co-develop high-quality commercial office assets in India's key markets. He said real estate investment strategies in India have historically focused on debt financing for residential developers or on acquiring core assets, and that the equity-led approach to office development gives investors an opportunity to participate in the value creation from high-quality projects favoured by corporates and global capability centres (GCCs). Lakshmi Iyer, managing director and chief executive of Bajaj Alts, said the first fund launch marks an important milestone in the company's journey and sets the foundation for building a broader and diversified alternatives platform for its investors. The fund will invest across select cities and sees GCCs and other large occupiers as one of its tailwinds. That demand is visible in market data: Cushman & Wakefield reported that gross office leasing across eight major cities rose 1 per cent to a record 64.6 million sq ft in January to September, and credited GCCs for the sustained activity, while Knight Frank put total leasing at a flat 66.7 million sq ft. The launch comes as private equity interest in office assets grows. Real estate consultant Anarock said private equity inflow into office assets rose 7 per cent to USD 945 million in the first half of the current fiscal year, as investors continued to buy completed, leased Grade A assets for stable rental income. Shobhit Agarwal, CEO of Anarock Capital, said investors are no longer just testing the waters and are committing larger cheques, taking equity positions and backing scalable platforms. Bajaj Alts has said its fund will take an equity-led route into office development, with GCCs and other large occupiers as one of its tailwinds. Source PTI
